title: London police officer cleared by SIU in shooting death of Justin Bourassa
subtitle: Police watchdog found no reasonable grounds to believe officer committed criminal offence
article: A London police officer who shot and killed 29-year-old Justin Bourassa last October will not be criminally charged in the death.
The Special Investigations Unit (SIU) said there are no reasonable grounds to believe that a London Police Service officer committed a criminal offence in the shooting on Oct. 28, 2021.

The SIU investigation revealed Bourassa was walking in the area of Richmond Street and Mill Street in London when he was stopped by LPS officers who were searching for suspects involved in a reported break and enter nearby.
The police watchdog said Bourassa was not involved in the suspected break in, but police wouldn't know this until after the incident.

"One officer held Mr. Bourassa while another officer approached with handcuffs. Mr. Bourassa broke free of the officer's grip and attempted to flee. The officers grabbed him and they fell to the ground. While on the ground, Mr. Bourassa choked one of the officers and the other officer fired at him and struck Mr. Bourassa," reads a statement issued by Joseph Martino, Director of the SIU.
Bourassa was taken to hospital where he was pronounced deceased.
The SIU has closed its investigation into the case.
Bourassa was from Sarnia, and was known for his love of tennis and connection to the francophone community.
"Justin was the tennis pro and beloved coach of the Sarnia Tennis Club. He took a special interest in teaching junior players, mentoring them to an elite level," Bourassa's obituary states.

"He was an exceptional athlete who loved cycling and running long distance. He was also a registered massage therapist who was highly respected in his field. Justin loved everyone and everyone loved him. He will be best remembered for his kindness to those less privileged, his gentleness, his humour and his joie de vivre."
A candlelight vigil was held for Bourassa at the Sarnia Tennis Club on Nov. 2, 2021.
